**Safest bet: Jackery HomePower 3000** if you want a full night even with a higher-draw queen blanket. One sizing guide estimates a queen blanket at 260 W and gives this 3,000 Wh station about **9.5 hours** of runtime; it lists the station at $1,499. [Check the sizing and runtime estimate](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/).

For a blanket that averages around **100 W**, a **1,000 Wh-class station** may be enough for roughly eight hours. For example, the [EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy) has 1,024 Wh—but it’s a less certain choice if your blanket draws more power or you use a high setting.

Check the blanket’s wattage label: runtime depends heavily on its actual draw and how much it cycles on and off. As a rough rule, look for **about 1,000 Wh for an eight-hour night at 100 W**, or closer to **2,600 Wh for eight hours at 260 W**. Keep the power station off the bed and plug the blanket directly into it.
